## Functions

### assert

Throws unless `value` is what the schema describes. After it returns the value is typed, with no
new binding: this is `check` for code that has nothing to do on a no but stop.

```ts
function assert<T>(schema: Schema<T, unknown>, value: unknown): asserts value is T;
```

| Parameter | Type |
| :-- | :-- |
| `schema` | `Schema<T, unknown>` |
| `value` | `unknown` |

**Returns** `asserts value is T`

### parseAsync

`parse`, awaited: the value the schema produces from `value`, or every reason there is none,
having awaited every rule and every map that answers with a promise. A schema with none of
those parses to what `parse` gives.

```ts
function parseAsync<T, O>(schema: Schema<T, O>, value: unknown, options?: ParseOptions): Promise<Parsed<Out<T, O>>>;
```

| Parameter | Type |
| :-- | :-- |
| `schema` | `Schema<T, O>` |
| `value` | `unknown` |
| `options` (optional) | `ParseOptions` |

**Returns** `Promise<Parsed<Out<T, O>>>`

## Constants

### annotate

The same schema with a title, a description or examples on it. Nothing that validates reads them.

```ts
const annotate: <S extends AnySchema>(schema: S, meta: Meta) => S;
```

### any

```ts
const any: () => Schema<any>;
```

### array

```ts
const array: <T, O>(item: Schema<T, O>, options?: ArrayOptions) => Schema<T[], [O] extends [Same] ? Same : O[]>;
```

### bigint

A bigint. Its bounds are bigints, which a double cannot hold, so they are kept as given, in
`value`; a bound nobody set is an infinity, which every bigint is inside.

```ts
const bigint: (options?: BigintOptions) => Schema<bigint>;
```

### boolean

```ts
const boolean: (options?: BooleanOptions) => Schema<boolean>;
```

### brand

The same schema, with a brand on its type: a `string` branded `'UserId'` is not assignable from a
plain `string`, so only a value that passed this schema can be used as one. Type only, as
`readonly` is: the node is the one it was given. The brand is on the input type too, which is
what a passing `check` narrows to.

```ts
const brand: <T, O, const B extends string | symbol>(schema: Schema<T, O>, _name: B) => Schema<T & Brand<B>, [O] extends [Same] ? Same : O & Brand<B>>;
```

### catchOf

The schema, and what `parse` reads in place of a value it refuses: `fallback`, or what a function
makes of the schema's issues. The fallback stands for an input, as a default does: it is held to
the schema and mapped by its transforms, so `catchOf(transform(string(), Number), '0')` hands out
0. `check`, `issues` and the input type still describe what the schema accepts: a fallback is a
thing `parse` does, as coercion is.

```ts
const catchOf: <T, O>(schema: Schema<T, O>, fallback: T | ((issues: readonly Issue[]) => T)) => Schema<T, Out<T, O>>;
```

### check

Whether `value` is what the schema describes. A type guard, so a passing check narrows.

```ts
const check: <T>(schema: Schema<T, unknown>, value: unknown) => value is T;
```

### codec

Two schemas and the two maps between them: `parse` reads a value with `input`, decodes it and
holds the result to `output`; `encode` does the same the other way. An ISO date string and a
`Date`, cents and a decimal string: one place says both directions. `check` describes what goes
in, which is the input schema alone, as it does for a pipe.

```ts
const codec: <I, IO, O, OO>(input: Schema<I, IO>, output: Schema<O, OO>, maps: CodecMaps<Out<I, IO>, Out<O, OO>>) => Codec<I, Out<O, OO>>;
```

### contains

The array schema, and at least one of its items is what `match` describes: JSON Schema's
`contains`, with `min` and `max` as its `minContains` and `maxContains`. The items are still each
held to the array's own item schema; `match` only counts.

```ts
const contains: <T extends readonly unknown[], O>(schema: Schema<T, O>, match: AnySchema, options?: ContainsOptions) => Schema<T, O>;
```

### custom

A type that is whatever a named predicate says it is (spec.md R10). The static type is the caller's to state.

```ts
const custom: <T>(name: string, test: Test) => Schema<T>;
```

### date

A `Date` that is a time: `new Date(NaN)` fails, and so does a string or a number that could be read as one.

```ts
const date: (options?: DateOptions) => Schema<Date>;
```

### discriminated

One object schema per value of `tag`, which is the case's key in `cases` and so a string. The
case is picked by that value, never by trying each.

```ts
const discriminated: <const C extends Cases>(tag: string, cases: C) => Schema<C[keyof C]["~type"], AnyOut<C[keyof C]>>;
```

### discriminatedBy

The same, for tags that are strings, numbers or booleans (parity.md decision 9): each case is an
object whose `tag` key is a literal, and that literal is its tag. A builder of its own, so that a
program whose tags are all strings does not carry the reading of them.

```ts
const discriminatedBy: <const C extends Schemas>(tag: string, cases: C) => Schema<C[number]["~type"], AnyOut<C[number]>>;
```

### encode

The other direction of a codec: a value of its output schema, held to that schema, encoded, and
the result held to the input schema. `parse` is the first direction, decoding.

```ts
const encode: <I, O>(schema: Codec<I, O>, value: unknown, options?: ParseOptions) => Parsed<I>;
```

### endsWith

The string schema, and the string ends with `text`.

```ts
const endsWith: <T extends string, O>(schema: Schema<T, O>, text: string) => Schema<T, O>;
```

```ts
const enumOf: <const T extends readonly (string | number)[]>(values: T) => Schema<T[number]>;
```

### exactOptional

Marks an object's field as one that may be absent and, when it is there, is not `undefined`
(`optional` reads `undefined` as absent, parity.md decision 2). A key the prototype holds counts
as there, as it does for a required field (decision 3).

```ts
const exactOptional: <T, O>(schema: Schema<T, O>) => OptionalSchema<T, O, T, never>;
```

### extend

The schema with more keys. One it already has is replaced where it stood, as a spread would.

```ts
const extend: <T, O, const S extends Shape>(schema: Schema<T, O>, shape: S) => Schema<Flat<Omit<T, keyof S> & ObjectOf<S>>, [O | S[keyof S]["~out"]] extends [Same] ? Same : Flat<Omit<Out<T, O>, keyof S> & ObjectFull<S>>>;
```

### func

Any function. What it takes and returns is not checked, since that cannot be known without
calling it: typebox reads a function schema the same way, and zod, valibot and arktype wrap the
function to check each call, which is another thing than validating a value.

```ts
const func: () => Schema<(...args: never[]) => unknown>;
```


```ts

```

### isMapped

A transform describes what goes in: `check` asks the schema it wraps, and never runs the map.
The same holds of every schema that only adds something for `parse` or for `issues` to what it
wraps: a pipe's second schema, a function run before validation, a message, a rule that is awaited.

```ts
const isMapped: (schema: Node, value: unknown) => boolean;
```

### isMultiple

Whether `value` is a multiple of `step`. The remainder is exact, so for a whole `step` it must be
zero. A fraction such as 0.1 has no exact double, and neither has 0.3, so there a value counts as a
multiple when it is within one rounding error of one: `|value| × Number.EPSILON`, which is the
most the two doubles can be off by together. So 0.3 and 0.1 + 0.2 are multiples of 0.1, as they are in the
decimal text of a JSON document, and 0.35 is not.

```ts
const isMultiple: (value: number, step: number) => boolean;
```

### issues

The second pass (spec.md R6, R7): every reason `value` is not what the schema describes. Empty
exactly when `check` says yes.

```ts
const issues: <T>(schema: Schema<T, unknown>, value: unknown, options?: IssueOptions) => Issue[];
```

### isTemplate

A string a template describes. The template is read as a machine with no memory but the set of
places it may stand at (Thompson's construction, 1968), one UTF-16 unit of the string at a time:
the time is the length of the string times the size of the template, whatever the string. A
regular expression made from the same template backtracks where two holes of open length follow
each other, and this never does.

```ts
const isTemplate: (schema: Node, value: unknown) => boolean;
```

### isTuple

An array of exactly the schema's items (parity.md decision 12: a tuple is closed), or of those
and then any number that match the schema in `item`.

```ts
const isTuple: (schema: Node, value: unknown) => boolean;
```

One of the schema's keys, as a string.

### keysOf

The keys a JSON Pointer names (RFC 6901 §4), in order: an issue's `path` as an array. Given the
value the issue is about, a key that is an index into an array is a number, as zod writes a
path; without it, and under a `Map` or a `Set`, every key is a string.

```ts
const keysOf: (path: string, value?: unknown) => (string | number)[];
```

```ts

```

A `Map` whose keys match one schema and whose values match another.

```ts
const mapOf: <K, KO, V, VO>(key: Schema<K, KO>, value: Schema<V, VO>) => Schema<Map<K, V>, [KO | VO] extends [Same] ? Same : Map<Out<K, KO>, Out<V, VO>>>;
```

### matching

How many of the items a schema accepts.

```ts
const matching: (schema: Node, items: readonly unknown[]) => number;
```

### message

The schema, with your words for its issues: one message for every issue it reports, or one for
each keyword you name (`{ type: '…', min: '…' }`). The words replace the whole message, `fix:`
line included, and stand whatever a per-call `message` hook says: the schema's own words are the
more specific. Only the wrapped schema's own issues are reworded, those reported where it stands
and those about one of its keys (`required`, `unknown`, `undefined`, `key`, `tag`); a schema
inside it keeps its own.

```ts
const message: <T, O>(schema: Schema<T, O>, words: string | Readonly<Record<string, string>>) => Schema<T, O>;
```

### nan

`NaN`, and no other number: `number()` refuses it, as JSON does.

```ts
const nan: () => Schema<number>;
```

### nativeEnum

The values of a TypeScript `enum`. A numeric enum compiles to an object that also maps each
number back to its name (`{ A: 0, 0: 'A' }`), and those names are not values: `0` is accepted
and `'A'` is not. A key is such a way back when its value is a name whose own value is that key;
to the type, it is a key that is a number.

```ts
const nativeEnum: <const T extends EnumObject>(members: T) => Schema<T[keyof T & string]>;
```

### never

Accepts no value.

```ts
const never: () => Schema<never>;
```

### normalize

The string in a Unicode normalization form (UAX #15, `String.prototype.normalize`): NFC unless another is named.

```ts
const normalize: <T extends string, M extends string | Same = Same>(schema: Text<T, M>, form?: NormalForm) => Schema<T, string>;
```

### not

Every value the schema refuses: JSON Schema's `not`. The type is `unknown`, since a type cannot
say "everything but"; narrow it with an intersection, `intersection([string(), not(literal(''))])`.

```ts
const not: (schema: AnySchema) => Schema<unknown>;
```

### nullable

`T` or `null`.

```ts
const nullable: <T, O>(schema: Schema<T, O>) => Schema<T | null, [O] extends [Same] ? Same : O | null>;
```

### nullish

`T`, `null` or `undefined`; as an object's field, the key may be absent.

```ts
const nullish: <T, O>(schema: Schema<T, O>) => OptionalSchema<T | null | undefined, [O] extends [Same] ? Same : O | null | undefined, T | null | undefined>;
```

### number

A finite number: `NaN` and the infinities fail, as they do in JSON.

```ts
const number: (options?: NumberOptions) => Schema<number>;
```

### object

```ts
const object: ObjectBuilder;
```

### omit

Every key but the named ones.

```ts
const omit: <T, O, const K extends keyof T & string>(schema: Schema<T, O>, keys: readonly K[]) => Schema<Omit<T, K>, [O] extends [Same] ? Same : Omit<O, K>>;
```

### oneOf

What exactly one member accepts: JSON Schema's `oneOf`, an exclusive or. A value two members
accept fails, which a union would let through. Every member is asked, so this costs more than a
union, which stops at the first that accepts; use it where two must not both hold.

```ts
const oneOf: <const T extends Schemas>(members: T) => Schema<T[number]["~type"], AnyOut<T[number]>>;
```

### optional

Marks an object's field as one that may be absent or `undefined`. It says that of the key, not of
the value: anywhere else (at the root, in an array, a tuple or a record) the schema is what it
was, so `check(optional(string()), undefined)` is false and the type says so. A value that may
itself be `undefined` is `nullish`, or a union with `literal(undefined)`.

```ts
const optional: OptionalBuilder;
```

### parse

The value the schema produces from `value`, or every reason there is none. `value` is the input
itself unless a default, a stripped key, a coercion or a transform changed something, or `copy`
was asked for.

```ts
const parse: <T, O>(schema: Schema<T, O>, value: unknown, options?: ParseOptions) => Parsed<Out<T, O>>;
```

### partial

Every key optional: absent or `undefined`. A field keeps its default.

```ts
const partial: <T, O>(schema: Schema<T, O>) => Schema<Loose<T>, [O] extends [Same] ? Same : Loose<O>>;
```

### pick

Only the named keys. A name the schema does not have is no key of the result.

```ts
const pick: <T, O, const K extends keyof T & string>(schema: Schema<T, O>, keys: readonly K[]) => Schema<Pick<T, K>, [O] extends [Same] ? Same : Pick<O, K & keyof O>>;
```

### pipe

Two schemas in a row: what `parse` makes of the first is parsed by the second, and what the
second makes of it is the output. `transform` maps a value and trusts the result; a pipe holds
the result to a schema: `pipe(transform(string(), Number), number({ min: 5 }))`.

```ts
const pipe: <T, M, U, R>(first: Schema<T, M>, second: Schema<U, R>) => Schema<T, Out<U, R>>;
```

### points

The number of code points in a string, which is what a length bound counts (parity.md decision 4:
JSON Schema's `minLength` and `maxLength`, zod and ajv). A surrogate pair is one; a surrogate
with no partner is one.

```ts
const points: (text: string) => number;
```

### preprocess

The schema, and a function `parse` runs on what arrived before anything is validated: a coercion
of your own. `transform` runs after validation, on a value of the schema's type; this runs
before it, on a value of any type, and what it returns is validated.

```ts
const preprocess: <T, O>(map: (value: unknown) => unknown, schema: Schema<T, O>) => Schema<T, O>;
```

### promise

A `Promise`. What it resolves to is not checked: that is only known later, and `check` answers
now. valibot, arktype and typebox read a promise schema the same way.

```ts
const promise: () => Schema<Promise<unknown>>;
```

### properties

The schema, held to a number of keys: JSON Schema's `minProperties` and `maxProperties`, for an
object or a record. The keys are counted as a record's are read, so an enumerable key of the
prototype counts (parity.md decision 3). A wrapper and not an option of `object`, so an object
that does not count its keys pays nothing for those that do.

```ts
const properties: <T extends object, O>(schema: Schema<T, O>, options: PropertiesOptions) => Schema<T, O>;
```

### readonly

The same schema, typed read-only, and marked `readOnly` for the JSON Schema and OpenAPI it is
written to: the value is the server's to set. Nothing is frozen: `parse` hands back the caller's
own value when nothing changed (parity.md decision 10), and freezing that would write to it. Of
the five libraries only zod freezes; valibot, arktype and typebox mark the type alone, as this does.

```ts
const readonly: <T, O>(schema: Schema<T, O>) => Schema<Readonly<T>, [O] extends [Same] ? Same : Readonly<O>>;
```

### record

An object with any keys, each value matching one schema. With an enum for `key` only its members
are keys, and none of them has to be there: `recordOf` is the record that needs every one.

```ts
const record: <V, O, K extends string = string>(value: Schema<V, O>, options?: RecordOptions<K>) => Schema<RecordOf<K, V>, [O] extends [Same] ? Same : RecordOf<K, O>>;
```

### recordOf

A record with exactly these keys, every one of them there, each value matching one schema: a closed object, written once.

```ts
const recordOf: <const K extends string, V, O>(keys: readonly K[], value: Schema<V, O>) => Schema<Record<K, V>, [O] extends [Same] ? Same : Record<K, O>>;
```

### refine

The schema, and a rule of your own on top of it (spec.md R10). The rule is handed what the
schema accepted, so it can rely on the type; it returns true for a value it allows.

```ts
const refine: <T, O, const K extends keyof T & string = never>(schema: Schema<T, O>, test: (value: NoInfer<[K] extends [never] ? T : Pick<T, K>>) => boolean, options?: RefineOptions<K>) => Schema<T, O>;
```

### refineAsync

The schema, and a rule of your own that answers with a promise: a lookup, a call to a service.
`parseAsync` awaits it, on a value the whole schema accepted and before any transform runs, and
reports it under the keyword `refine`. `parse` refuses a schema that has one.

```ts
const refineAsync: <T, O>(schema: Schema<T, O>, test: (value: T) => Promise<boolean>, options?: RefineAsyncOptions) => Schema<T, O>;
```

### repeated

The index of the first item that is the same value as an earlier one, or -1. A value that is no
object is looked up in a set, so an array of strings and numbers is read in time proportional to
its length. An object is compared with every object before it: for an array of `k` objects that
is `k × (k - 1) / 2` comparisons at worst, each as deep as the objects are alike.

```ts
const repeated: (items: readonly unknown[]) => number;
```

### required

Every key required: there, and not `undefined`.

```ts
const required: <T, O>(schema: Schema<T, O>) => Schema<Present<T>, [O] extends [Same] ? Same : Present<O>>;
```

### safeInteger

An integer every double can tell from its neighbours: from `Number.MIN_SAFE_INTEGER` to
`Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, so 2 ** 53 fails (parity.md decision 5: `number({ int: true })` is any
integer-valued double). The safe range is put into the node's own two bounds, so `check` tests
nothing it did not test already, and a builder of its own, so `number` is no larger for it.

```ts
const safeInteger: (options?: Omit<NumberOptions, "int">) => Schema<number>;
```

### setOf

A `Set` whose members each match one schema; `min` and `max` bound its size.

```ts
const setOf: <T, O>(item: Schema<T, O>, options?: ArrayOptions) => Schema<Set<T>, [O] extends [Same] ? Same : Set<O>>;
```

### startsWith

The string schema, and the string starts with `text`: a prefix, without a regular expression of yours to escape.

```ts
const startsWith: <T extends string, O>(schema: Schema<T, O>, text: string) => Schema<T, O>;
```

### string

```ts
const string: (options?: StringOptions) => Schema<string>;
```

### symbol

```ts
const symbol: () => Schema<symbol>;
```

### template

A string made of text and holes, as TypeScript's template literal types make one:
`template(['user-', number({ int: true })])` accepts `user-7` and is typed `` `user-${number}` ``.
A hole holds a string, a number, a bigint, a boolean, or a literal, an enum, a union or a nullable
of those, with no bounds: what it matches is the text `String` writes for such a value. A number
is written as JSON writes one, so `1e+21` matches and `0x10` does not.

```ts
const template: <const P extends readonly (string | AnySchema)[]>(parts: P) => Schema<TemplateOf<P>>;
```

### transform

The schema, and a function that makes of what it accepts what `parse` hands out (spec.md R10).
`check`, `issues` and the input type describe what goes in; only `parse` runs the function, and
only on a value the whole schema accepted.

```ts
const transform: <T, M, R>(schema: Schema<T, M>, map: (value: Out<T, M>) => R) => Schema<T, R>;
```

### transformAsync

The schema, and a function that answers with a promise of what `parseAsync` hands out. It runs
as a transform does: after validation, on what the schema it wraps produced. `parse` refuses a
schema that has one.

```ts
const transformAsync: <T, M, R>(schema: Schema<T, M>, map: (value: Out<T, M>) => Promise<R>) => Schema<T, R>;
```

### trim

The string with the white space at its two ends removed (`String.prototype.trim`). Like every
transform it runs after validation: the schema describes the string as it arrives. To hold the
trimmed string to a schema, `pipe(trim(string()), string({ min: 1 }))`.

```ts
const trim: <T extends string, M extends string | Same = Same>(schema: Text<T, M>) => Schema<T, string>;
```

### tuple

Exactly these items, in this order: one more or one fewer fails (parity.md decision 12). With
`rest`, any number of further items, each matching that schema.

```ts
const tuple: TupleBuilder;
```

### undefinedOf

Only `undefined`: the literal with no value. As an object's field it is a key that must be absent or `undefined`, so mark it `optional`.

```ts
const undefinedOf: () => Schema<undefined>;
```

### union

What any one member accepts. The members are tried in order, and the first to accept decides what `parse` returns.

```ts
const union: <const T extends Schemas>(members: T) => Schema<T[number]["~type"], AnyOut<T[number]>>;
```

### unique

The array schema, and no two of its items are the same value: JSON Schema's `uniqueItems`. Arrays
and plain objects are compared by what they hold, in any key order; a date by its time; `NaN` is
the same as `NaN`. Any other object is the same only as itself (check.ts, `sameValue`).

```ts
const unique: <T extends readonly unknown[], O>(schema: Schema<T, O>) => Schema<T, O>;
```

### unknown

Accepts every value. `any` is the same node with the type that switches checking off.

```ts
const unknown: () => Schema<unknown>;
```

### uppercase

The string in upper case (`String.prototype.toUpperCase`).

```ts
const uppercase: <T extends string, M extends string | Same = Same>(schema: Text<T, M>) => Schema<T, string>;
```

### voidOf

Only `undefined`, typed `void`: what a function that returns nothing returns. The same node as `undefinedOf`.

```ts
const voidOf: () => Schema<void>;
```

## Interfaces

### ArrayOptions

```ts
interface ArrayOptions {
    readonly min?: number;
    readonly max?: number;
}
```

### BigintOptions

```ts
interface BigintOptions {
    readonly min?: bigint;
    readonly max?: bigint;
}
```

### BooleanOptions

```ts
interface BooleanOptions {
    /** `parse` reads the boolean from the string `true` or `false`, exactly. `check` never does. */
    readonly coerce?: boolean;
}
```

### Brand

What a brand adds to a type: a member no value has, named by the brand. Two brands on one type are both there.

```ts
interface Brand<B extends string | symbol> {
    readonly '~brand': {
        readonly [K in B]: true;
    };
}
```

### Codec

A schema with two directions: `parse` decodes what arrives into the output, and `encode` turns an output back into what was sent.

```ts
interface Codec<I, O> extends Schema<I, O> {
    readonly '~codec': true;
}
```

### CodecMaps

```ts
interface CodecMaps<I, O> {
    /** From what the input schema accepted, to a value for the output schema. */
    readonly decode: (value: I) => unknown;
    /** From what the output schema accepted, to a value for the input schema. */
    readonly encode: (value: O) => unknown;
}
```

### ContainsOptions

```ts
interface ContainsOptions {
    /** The fewest items the schema has to accept: 1 unless another is given, and 0 makes the test always hold. */
    readonly min?: number;
    /** The most it may accept. */
    readonly max?: number;
}
```

### DateOptions

```ts
interface DateOptions {
    /**
     * `parse` reads the date from a string that is, whole, an RFC 3339 date-time (`2020-01-01T00:00:00Z`,
     * with any offset and any fraction) or full-date (`2020-01-01`, read as midnight UTC). `check` never does.
     */
    readonly coerce?: boolean;
}
```

### DefaultedSchema

A field whose key may be absent going in, and is always there coming out of `parse`: an optional
with a default. Its output type is always written out, which is what tells an object that its
own output is not its input.

```ts
interface DefaultedSchema<T, O = T> extends Schema<T, O> {
    readonly '~optional': T | undefined;
}
```

### Invalid

What `assert` throws: a `TypeError` whose message is the first issue, carrying every one of them.

```ts
interface Invalid extends TypeError {
    readonly issues: readonly Issue[];
}
```

### Issue

```ts
interface Issue {
    /** JSON Pointer to the value that failed; `''` is the root. */
    readonly path: string;
    /**
     * What failed: `type`, `min`, `max`, `gt`, `lt`, `integer`, `multipleOf`, `pattern`, `format`,
     * `literal`, `enum`, `required`, `unknown`, `key`, `length`, `tag`, `union`, `never`, `custom`,
     * `date`, `instance`, `undefined`, `refine`, `minProperties`, `maxProperties`.
     */
    readonly keyword: string;
    /** What was expected and what arrived, ending in a `fix:` line; or the words a schema was given with `message`. */
    readonly message: string;
}
```

### IssueOptions

```ts
interface IssueOptions {
    /** Stop at the first issue. */
    readonly first?: boolean;
    /**
     * The message for an issue, in your words or your language. It is asked about every issue of
     * every schema, and what it returns is the whole message. Where it returns nothing the message
     * stays as it was, with its `fix:` line: a map can cover the keywords it knows and leave the rest.
     */
    readonly message?: (miss: Miss) => string | null | undefined;
}
```

### Meta

What a schema says about itself. Carried on the node and read back; validation ignores it.

```ts
interface Meta {
    readonly title?: string;
    readonly description?: string;
    readonly examples?: readonly unknown[];
    /** The value is the server's to set and a client's to leave out: OpenAPI's and JSON Schema's `readOnly`, which `readonly` sets. */
    readonly readOnly?: boolean;
}
```

### Miss

One failed expectation at one place, before it is put into words: what a message is made from.

```ts
interface Miss {
    readonly path: string;
    readonly keyword: string;
    /** What was expected, in English: the message reads "expected <expected>, got …". */
    readonly expected: string;
    /** The value that arrived. */
    readonly got: unknown;
    /** What to do about it, in English: the message ends "fix: <fix>". */
    readonly fix: string;
}
```

### Node

```ts
interface Node {
    readonly kind: Kind;
    /** The kind's own check, put here by the builder so that a bundle carries only the kinds it builds. It captures nothing. */
    readonly check: Check;
    /** Length for a string or an array, value for a number, size for a set, the number of keys for a count of them. */
    readonly min: number;
    readonly max: number;
    /** A number's exclusive bounds: the infinities when there are none. */
    readonly above: number;
    readonly below: number;
    /** What a number must be a multiple of; zero when it need not be. */
    readonly step: number;
    readonly int: boolean;
    /** `parse` reads the value from a string: a number from a JSON number, a boolean from `true` or `false`, a date from an RFC 3339 date or date-time. */
    readonly coerce: boolean;
    readonly pattern: RegExp | null;
    /** A string's format, a custom type's predicate, or a refinement's rule: its name is what the rule expects. */
    readonly rule: Rule | null;
    /**
     * The literal's value; a bigint's two bounds, lowest first; the name `typeof` gives the values of
     * a `type` node; the class an `instance` node's values are instances of; a transform's map; the
     * function a `preprocess` node runs first; the words of a `message` node, one string or one a keyword;
     * the rule or the map that `parseAsync` awaits.
     */
    readonly value: unknown;
    /** The enum's members; on an object that closes or strips, its keys; on a refinement, the keys its rule reads. */
    readonly values: ReadonlySet<unknown> | null;
    /**
     * The array's or the set's element, the record's or the map's value, the schema of an object's
     * unnamed keys or of a tuple's items past its last, or what a schema that wraps another wraps: for
     * a pipe, its first schema.
     */
    readonly item: Node | null;
    /** The record's or the map's key; a pipe's second schema. */
    readonly key: Node | null;
    /** The object's keys and, in the same order, their schemas; on a refinement, the path its issue is reported at. */
    readonly keys: readonly string[] | null;
    /** An object's fields, a tuple's items, or the members of a union or an intersection. */
    readonly fields: readonly Node[] | null;
    /** On an object's field: the key may be absent. `'exact'` is absent or a value, and never `undefined`. */
    readonly optional: boolean | 'exact';
    /** What `parse` puts where `undefined` arrived; `undefined` when there is none. */
    readonly default: unknown;
    readonly unknown: Unknown;
    /** The discriminated union's key and its cases by that key's value: a string, a number or a boolean (parity.md decision 9). */
    readonly tag: string | null;
    readonly cases: ReadonlyMap<unknown, Node> | null;
    /** A lazy node's schema, asked for when it is read: what lets a schema name itself. */
    readonly get: (() => Node) | null;
    readonly meta: Meta | null;
    /** The kind's own reading for `issues` and `parse`; null for the eight kinds they read themselves. */
    readonly own: Own | null;
}
```

### NumberOptions

```ts
interface NumberOptions {
    readonly min?: number;
    readonly max?: number;
    /** Exclusive bounds: the bound itself fails. */
    readonly gt?: number;
    readonly lt?: number;
    /** Above zero; `negative` is below zero. Zero is neither. */
    readonly positive?: boolean;
    readonly negative?: boolean;
    /** See `isMultiple` in check.ts for what a multiple of a fraction is. */
    readonly multipleOf?: number;
    readonly int?: boolean;
    /** `parse` reads the number from a string that is a JSON number. `check` never does. */
    readonly coerce?: boolean;
}
```

### ObjectOptions

```ts
interface ObjectOptions<U> {
    /**
     * Keys the shape does not name: `'keep'` allows them and leaves them alone (the default, parity.md
     * decision 1), `'strict'` refuses them, `'strip'` allows them and `parse` leaves them out of its
     * output, and a schema is what each of their values must match.
     */
    readonly unknown?: U;
}
```

### OptionalOptions

```ts
interface OptionalOptions<T> {
    /**
     * What `parse` puts where the value is absent or `undefined`. It stands for the input that was
     * not there, so it is then read as an input is: coerced, filled and mapped by this schema where
     * the schema does those things, and otherwise handed out as it is, uncopied. Freeze an object
     * you give here. `check` and the input type still describe the input, where the key may be absent.
     */
    readonly default?: T;
}
```

### OptionalSchema

A field whose key may be absent. `F` is what the key may hold when it is there, which for
`optional` is the schema's own type or `undefined` (parity.md decision 2), and `G` is what it
may hold coming out of `parse` beside the schema's output: `undefined`, or for an exact key nothing.

```ts
interface OptionalSchema<T, O = Same, F = T | undefined, G = undefined> extends Schema<T, O> {
    readonly '~optional': F;
    readonly '~absent': G;
}
```

### Own

What a kind brings for `issues` and for `parse`, when they do not know the kind themselves. They
know the eight kinds the design's first step named (string, number, boolean, literal, enum, array,
object, discriminated); every other kind's builder puts this on its node, as it puts `check`.
So `issues` and `parse` do not grow with the number of kinds, and a bundle carries the reading
of the kinds it builds.

```ts
interface Own {
    readonly issues: Reader;
    readonly fill: Filler;
}
```

### ParseOptions

```ts
interface ParseOptions extends IssueOptions {
    /**
     * Hand out a new object or array for every one the schema describes, changed or not, as zod and
     * valibot always do. Without it the input itself comes back wherever nothing changed. What an
     * `unknown` schema lets through is never copied: nothing describes it.
     */
    readonly copy?: boolean;
}
```

### Pass

One walk of `parse` over a value. It makes two: one before `check`, and one after it when there is a transform to run.

```ts
interface Pass {
    /** The walk after `check`: every value is one its schema accepted, and transforms run. */
    late: boolean;
    /** Every object and array the schema describes is rebuilt, changed or not. */
    readonly copy: boolean;
    /** Set by the first walk when it meets a transform: what makes the second worth making. */
    met: boolean;
    /** The way of `parse` into a schema inside this one, handed over as a walk's `visit` is. */
    readonly fill: Filler;
    /** Where the walk is: the keys from the root to the member being filled. */
    readonly at: unknown[];
    /** What the walk after `check` found wrong: the issues of a pipe's second schema. One of them fails the parse. */
    readonly failed: Issue[];
    /** `parse` itself and the options it was called with, for a schema that parses what another produced. */
    readonly parse: (schema: Node, value: unknown, options: IssueOptions) => {
        readonly ok: true;
        readonly value: unknown;
    } | {
        readonly ok: false;
        readonly issues: Issue[];
    };
    readonly options: IssueOptions;
    /** Set by `parseAsync` alone: a schema that has to be awaited refuses a walk without it, and a rule that is awaited counts itself here. */
    readonly wait?: {
        rules: number;
    };
}
```

### PropertiesOptions

```ts
interface PropertiesOptions {
    /** The fewest and the most keys the object may have. */
    readonly min?: number;
    readonly max?: number;
}
```

### RecordOptions

```ts
interface RecordOptions<K extends string = string> {
    /** What every key must be. A key is always a string, so this is a string schema or an enum of strings. */
    readonly key?: Schema<K>;
}
```

### RefineAsyncOptions

```ts
interface RefineAsyncOptions {
    /** Where under the value the issue is reported: the keys that lead there. The value itself when there are none. */
    readonly path?: readonly (string | number)[];
    /** What the rule expects, for the issue: it reads "expected <message>, got …". */
    readonly message?: string;
}
```

### RefineOptions

```ts
interface RefineOptions<K extends string = string> {
    /** Where under the value the issue is reported: the keys that lead there. The value itself when there are none. */
    readonly path?: readonly (string | number)[];
    /** What the rule expects, for the issue: it reads "expected <message>, got …". */
    readonly message?: string;
    /**
     * The keys of the object that the rule reads. With them the rule runs whenever those fields are
     * sound, whatever is wrong with the others, and is handed a value typed with those keys alone.
     * Without them it runs only on a value that is sound all through.
     */
    readonly uses?: readonly K[];
}
```

### Rule

A named rule, as data (spec.md R11): a string's format, or the whole of a custom type. One of `pattern` and `test` is set.

```ts
interface Rule {
    readonly name: string;
    readonly pattern: RegExp | null;
    readonly test: Test | null;
}
```

### Same

What stands where a schema's output type would, when its output is its input. That is nearly
every schema, and it is why the type of an object is worked out once and not twice: measured
2026-11-13 with TypeScript 6.0.3 on 200 copies of the order schema, carrying a second, equal
type cost 725 instantiations a schema against 420, and this costs 461.

```ts
interface Same {
    readonly '~same': never;
}
```

### Schema

A node that validates a `T`, and from which `parse` produces an `O`: `Same` unless a default
fills a key or a transform maps a value somewhere inside. The types live only in the type system.

```ts
interface Schema<T, O = Same> extends Node {
    readonly '~type': T;
    readonly '~out': O;
}
```

### StringOptions

```ts
interface StringOptions {
    /** Code points, not UTF-16 units (parity.md decision 4). */
    readonly min?: number;
    readonly max?: number;
    readonly length?: number;
    readonly pattern?: RegExp;
    readonly format?: Format;
}
```

### Walk

Where a walk of `issues` is, and where it writes. It also holds the two things of `issues` that a
reader calls, the way into a schema inside this one and the writing down of an issue, so that a
reader a node carries imports neither and a bundle without `issues` does not carry them.

```ts
interface Walk {
    readonly found: Issue[];
    readonly first: boolean;
    readonly message: IssueOptions['message'];
    readonly visit: Reader;
    readonly add: (walk: Walk, miss: Miss) => void;
}
```

## Types

### AllOf

What every one of the schemas validates at once.

```ts
type AllOf<T extends Schemas> = T extends readonly [Schema<infer First, unknown>, ...infer Rest extends Schemas] ? First & AllOf<Rest> : unknown;
```

### AllOut

```ts
type AllOut<T extends Schemas> = [T[number]['~out']] extends [Same] ? Same : AllFull<T>;
```

### AnyOut

The output type of a union of schemas, given as the union of their types.

```ts
type AnyOut<M extends AnySchema> = [M['~out']] extends [Same] ? Same : OutOf<M>;
```

### AnySchema

Any schema at all: the constraint for a function that takes one and does not care for its types.

```ts
type AnySchema = Schema<unknown, unknown>;
```

### Check

A schema is data (spec.md R1): every builder returns one frozen node, a kind and its constraints.
`check`, `issues`, `parse`, the code emitter and, later, the JSON Schema writer all read that node.

```ts
type Check = (schema: Node, value: unknown) => boolean;
```

### Filler

What `parse` runs for a kind: the value the schema makes of `value`, which is `value` itself when nothing changed.

```ts
type Filler = (schema: Node, value: unknown, pass: Pass) => unknown;
```

### Flat

```ts
type Flat<T> = {
    [K in keyof T]: T[K];
};
```

### Format

A string format, as data (spec.md R11): a name and either a pattern or a test. Nothing is
registered anywhere; a format is a value a program keeps and hands to `string({ format })`.

```ts
type Format = {
    readonly name: string;
    readonly pattern: RegExp;
} | {
    readonly name: string;
    readonly test: (value: string) => boolean;
};
```

### Infer

What `check` accepts, and narrows to: the input. `parse` reads a little more where a schema asks
for coercion (a number from a string), which no type can say, so the input type is `check`'s.

```ts
type Infer<S extends AnySchema> = S['~type'];
```

### InferInput

The same as `Infer`, under the name that pairs with `InferOutput`.

```ts
type InferInput<S extends AnySchema> = S['~type'];
```

### InferOutput

What `parse` produces: the input with every default filled and every transform applied.

```ts
type InferOutput<S extends AnySchema> = Out<S['~type'], S['~out']>;
```

### Kind

```ts
type Kind = 'string' | 'number' | 'boolean' | 'literal' | 'enum' | 'array' | 'object' | 'discriminated' | 'unknown' | 'never' | 'record' | 'tuple' | 'nullable' | 'nullish' | 'union' | 'intersection' | 'lazy' | 'custom' | 'bigint' | 'date' | 'type' | 'instance' | 'refine' | 'transform' | 'nan' | 'map' | 'set' | 'count' | 'message' | 'pipe' | 'preprocess' | 'refineAsync' | 'transformAsync' | 'template' | 'startsWith' | 'endsWith' | 'includes' | 'contains' | 'unique' | 'not' | 'oneOf' | 'catch' | 'codec';
```

### NormalForm

```ts
type NormalForm = 'NFC' | 'NFD' | 'NFKC' | 'NFKD';
```

### ObjectFull

An object as `parse` produces it, where that is not what went in: a key with a default is always there.

```ts
type ObjectFull<S extends Shape> = Flat<{
    [K in Exclude<keyof S, AbsentKeys<S>>]: OutOf<S[K]>;
} & {
    [K in AbsentKeys<S>]?: OutOf<S[K]> | (S[K] & MayStayAbsent)['~absent'];
}>;
```

### ObjectOf

```ts
type ObjectOf<S extends Shape> = Flat<{
    [K in Exclude<keyof S, OptionalKeys<S>>]: S[K]['~type'];
} & {
    [K in OptionalKeys<S>]?: (S[K] & MayBeAbsent)['~optional'];
}>;
```

### ObjectOut

An object's output type: `Same` when every field's is, and only otherwise worked out.

```ts
type ObjectOut<S extends Shape> = [S[keyof S]['~out']] extends [Same] ? Same : ObjectFull<S>;
```

### Out

The output type that a schema's two types stand for.

```ts
type Out<T, O> = [O] extends [Same] ? T : O;
```

### Parsed

The parse path: the value a schema's defaults, stripping and coercion produce, then `check` on
that value, then the schema's transforms on what `check` accepted. `check` itself stays a guard
that reads and never writes.

```ts
type Parsed<T> = {
    readonly ok: true;
    readonly value: T;
} | {
    readonly ok: false;
    readonly issues: Issue[];
};
```

### Reader

What `issues` runs for a kind: it writes down every reason `got` is not what the schema describes.

```ts
type Reader = (walk: Walk, schema: Node, got: unknown, path: string) => void;
```

### RecordOf

A record's type: any string as a key, or, when its keys are an enum, some of those and no other.

```ts
type RecordOf<K extends string, V> = string extends K ? Record<string, V> : {
    [P in K]?: V;
};
```

### Shape

```ts
type Shape = Readonly<Record<string, AnySchema>>;
```

### Step

One step of a template's reading: a UTF-16 unit from `low` to `high`, or, when `kind` is 1, a way on to two other steps, each so many steps from this one.

```ts
type Step = readonly [kind: number, low: number, high: number];
```

### TemplateOf

The string a template's parts describe.

```ts
type TemplateOf<P extends readonly unknown[]> = P extends readonly [infer First, ...infer Rest] ? `${PieceOf<First>}${TemplateOf<Rest>}` : '';
```

### Test

A predicate a node names (spec.md R10). Beside `check`, `get` and a transform's map, it is the only kind of function a node may hold.

```ts
type Test = (value: unknown) => boolean;
```

### TupleFull

```ts
type TupleFull<T extends Schemas> = {
    -readonly [K in keyof T]: OutOf<T[K]>;
};
```

### TupleOf

A tuple of schemas as the tuple of what they validate.

```ts
type TupleOf<T extends Schemas> = {
    -readonly [K in keyof T]: T[K]['~type'];
};
```

### TupleOut

```ts
type TupleOut<T extends Schemas> = [T[number]['~out']] extends [Same] ? Same : TupleFull<T>;
```

### Unknown

What an object does with a key its shape does not name. `strip` is `keep` to `check`: only `parse` leaves the key out.

```ts
type Unknown = 'keep' | 'strict' | 'strip';
```

Documented on the page of the entry point that declares them.

| Export | Kind | Documented in |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `VENDOR` | const | [`truefit/standard`](/docs/api/standard#vendor) |
